props.name: bounds
props.description: What bounds the Sidebar. `page` fills at least the viewport's height, fixes the desktop rail to the viewport, writes the open state to the `sidebar:state` cookie and toggles on ⌘B or Ctrl+B from anywhere in the document. `container` fills its container's height, which the host must define, keeps the rail inside it, writes no cookie, so a host that wants the state kept passes `open` and `onOpenChange`, and toggles on the shortcut only from a keydown inside the Provider's React tree, so a page Sidebar around it keeps the shortcut everywhere else. An `Inset` taller than the container is clipped, so the host scrolls the inset's own content. The mobile Sheet still follows the viewport's width.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: The desktop open state on first render. The Provider reads it once, so a later value changes nothing. A page Sidebar writes its state to the `sidebar:state` cookie on every change. To restore it without a flash, read that cookie in a server layout with `cookies()` and pass it here. A value read on the client arrives after hydration, which renders the server's value, so a client-only read has to control `open` instead.

props.name: labels
props.description: Text for the Trigger's and Rail's label and the mobile Sheet's screen reader title and description. Each one left out comes from the locale dictionary's `sidebar.*` entries.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the requested desktop open state. When you pass it, the Provider keeps no state of its own. At `bounds="page"` it still writes the cookie on every change.

props.name: onOpenMobileChange
props.description: Called with the requested Sheet state when the Trigger, the shortcut, the Sheet's own dismissal or `useSidebar().setOpenMobile` asks to open or close it. When you pass it, the Provider keeps no Sheet state of its own, and the host decides.

props.name: open
props.description: The desktop open state, for a Sidebar you control.

props.name: openMobile
props.description: The open state of the Sheet the Root becomes below 768px, so a host can close it from outside, such as after a navigation. It lasts for the session only and is never written to the cookie. Uncontrolled, it starts closed.

props.name: children
props.description: The rail's sections: `Sidebar.Header`, `Sidebar.Content`, `Sidebar.Footer` and `Sidebar.Rail`. Below 768px they show in a Sheet, under a close button.

props.name: collapsible
props.description: How the rail collapses. `offcanvas` slides it off the edge, `icon` narrows it to `--sidebar-width-icon` with only the icons showing, and `none` keeps it open. A `none` root still writes `data-state`, `data-variant` and `data-side` for an `inset` layout.

props.name: dir
props.description: The text direction of the mobile Sheet, such as `rtl`.

props.name: side
props.description: The edge the rail sits on. The root writes it as `data-side`. For `right`, keep the Root before `Sidebar.Inset` and pass `className="flex-row-reverse"` to `Sidebar.Provider`, so the rail's spacer moves to the right edge and the Inset still reads the Root's state.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles. The root's element props land on a different element in each layout: the rail container on desktop, the Sheet's dialog below 768px and the root `div` with `collapsible="none"`. In the Sheet, `style` merges over the mobile `--sidebar-width`, so it can set the Sheet's width.

props.name: variant
props.description: The rail style. `sidebar` sits flush with the edge behind a border. `floating` pads the rail and rounds and shadows its surface. `inset` pads the rail and shows the `Sidebar.Inset` beside it as a card.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element. The trigger's accessible name. Unset, it is the locale dictionary's `sidebar.toggle`.

props.name: children
props.description: The label and icons. Mark a leading icon with `data-icon="inline-start"` and a trailing one with `data-icon="inline-end"`, and that side takes the narrower icon padding. Your own icon components must pass `data-icon` through to the element they render. An SVG without a `size-*` class renders at 16px, or 12px at the `xs` and `icon-xs` sizes. Any `size-*` class opts out, `size-auto` included, and `w-*` or `h-*` alone does not. An SVG without a `viewBox` clips at that size instead of scaling. Give it `size-auto` to keep its own `width` and `height`, or restore the `viewBox`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes, merged last through `cn`. A `px-*` class replaces the label padding only. The icon side keeps its own padding, which `has-data-[icon=inline-start]:pl-*` or `has-data-[icon=inline-end]:pr-*` replaces.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description: Marks an action in flight. The button blocks activation, dims, and stamps `data-pending` and `aria-busy`. It stays in the focus order, so a keyboard user is still on it when the result arrives. `focusableWhenDisabled={false}` takes it out of the focus order. `aria-busy` announces nothing, so say what is happening in the label, such as "Saving", or in a `role="status"` region outside the button. Put a label that changes with the state in its own element, such as `{label}`: page translation replaces a bare text child with its own nodes, so React's update to the old text node never shows.

props.name: isVisuallyDisabled
props.description: Makes the button look and announce disabled while it stays interactive. It stamps `aria-disabled`, and an explicit `aria-disabled` wins. Click, keyboard and focus still work, and a Tooltip on the button still opens. Use it for an action that explains on activation why it is unavailable.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: onIntent
props.description: Fires once when the pointer's predicted path enters the inflated hit rect, for prefetching. Browsers without pointer prediction never fire it.

props.name: pendingIndicator
props.description: What a pending button shows in its leading icon position. When you omit it, a spinner shows there and the button's leading and bare icons hide, while a `data-icon="inline-end"` icon stays. A node replaces the spinner and does not animate on its own. `null` or `false` shows nothing and hides nothing, so the call site draws its own pending state. Fade that content with `group-data-pending/button:opacity-0`, not `invisible`, which drops the label from the accessible name, and give an overlay no `data-icon`.

props.name: predictionZoneSize
props.description: Pixels added to every side of the hit rect when predicting pointer intent.
